title: Can a curve learn coin flips?
hook: The labels are pure chance. Can a flexible curve still fit every one of them?

knows: that a model can overfit its training data
that a curve's degree sets how much it can bend
doesNotKnow: that a model with as many tunable numbers as data points can fit any labels, even random ones
that a perfect training fit is therefore not evidence of a pattern

misconception: If a model fits the training data perfectly, it must have found a pattern.
objective: The learner can say that enough freedom fits anything, including coin flips, so a zero training error alone does not show that a model learned a real pattern.

claims.text: The six points and their coin-flip labels are a toy, labelled 'Coin-flip labels · toy fit' on the stage. Label set n is drawn with mulberry32(n): set 1 is −1, 1, −1, −1, −1, 1; set 2 is −1, 1, 1, −1, −1, −1.
claims.source: Brief 50 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md (the brief's example labels 1, −1, −1, 1, 1, −1 were not used); labelsFor() in Demo.tsx. Seeds 1, 2, ... are taken in order, untuned.

claims.text: A degree-5 curve has six numbers to tune, so it passes through all six dots for any labels: its largest miss is 0.00.
claims.source: Polynomial interpolation: six distinct x values determine a unique degree-5 interpolant. fit() in Demo.tsx; node over label sets 1-1000: largest miss below 1e-10 in every set.

claims.text: On label set 1 the degree-1 line misses by up to 1.51 and the degree-3 curve by 0.76; the degree-5 fit's biggest coefficient is 833 (625 on set 2).
claims.source: report(set, deg) in Demo.tsx; node re-run: set 1 d1 1.505, d3 0.762, d5 0.000 (coef 833); set 2 d5 coef 625. Degree 3 misses some dot in 967 of 1000 label sets.

claims.text: Because the labels are coin flips, the fitted curve's guesses on new points are right only by chance (about half the time).
claims.source: By construction: a new point's label is an independent fair coin flip, so any guess matches it with probability 1/2 whatever the curve.

claims.text: Large neural networks have been shown to fit randomly shuffled labels perfectly too.
claims.source: About real systems: Zhang, Bengio, Hardt, Recht & Vinyals 2017, 'Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization', ICLR (image classifiers reach zero training error on CIFAR-10 with random labels).

recall.question: A model with millions of parameters reaches zero training error on your data. What does that alone tell you about whether it found a real pattern?
options: That it found one: a perfect fit proves it
Little: a model that flexible could fit even random labels; check it on held-out data
That the data has no pattern
recall.why: Enough freedom fits anything, including coin flips. Only performance on data the model did not see can show a pattern was learned.
